hook_text: Three boxes explain a mine winder to someone who has never seen a gear. Here is the systems diagram.
clip_script: Input, process, output. What goes in, what happens to it, what comes out. For a mechanism: a motion in, with its speed; the gears and their ratio in the middle; the new motion out. MA 4 to 1: 12T driving 48T. In: 400 rpm, weak, clockwise. Process: 4 to 1, direction flips. Out: 100 rpm, four times the torque, anticlockwise. Slow strong box: that is your winder. Now swap the driver. 48T drives 12T. In: 100 rpm strong. Out: 400 rpm, a quarter the torque. Fast weak box: that is a hand drill. Same gears, different driver, different machine. Ruled boxes, numbers on every arrow, a title that says the job. Chain the whole winder, battery to rising cage, with a brake box pointing at the drum, and you have the flow chart the tender board reads first.
visual_style: Three chalk boxes on a whiteboard fill with words and numbers; arrows carry 400 and 100 rpm; the diagram mirrors with 100 and 400; a long chain of boxes from battery to cage unrolls with a brake box pointing at the drum.
pacing: Three boxes, slow strong, fast weak, the chain.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the three boxes for your team's winder with real numbers.
